author: Mark Atwood
text:
Resolved: option (b) — extend mime-tree to expose typed header values, then jmap-mail-server consumes mime-tree's new API. jmap-mail-server does NOT take a direct dep on mail-parser; mime-tree remains the single workspace gateway to RFC 5322 parsing.

Rationale: mime-tree (at ~/PROJECT/MIME) is the in-house RFC 5322 parser. It already uses mail-parser internally but currently flattens parsed headers to ParsedHeader{name, value} strings before exposing them. The fix is to add a typed-header API to mime-tree (additive — no break), then consume it from jmap-mail-server. Single source of truth for header parsing in the workspace family; no new top-level dep.

Cross-repo work tracked at: MIME-vy5 (in ~/PROJECT/MIME bd database).

Sequence:
1. MIME-vy5 lands in mime-tree (typed header API + tests against independent RFC 5322 example vectors).
2. mime-tree minor version bumped.
3. JMAP-g7wu.5 unblocked; jmap-mail-server consumes the new API to implement the 5 As* header forms.
